Nature & food

tree frog noun

also green frog, tree frogs

post-classical

Plin. NH 32.122: ea rāna, quam Graecī calamītēn vocant
Plin. NH 32.139 (Lewis & Short)

calamītēs, calamītae m.

noun, first declension

Pliny’s name, from the Greek, for the smallest and greenest of the frogs, which lives among reeds and bushes

Lewis & Short calls it the green frog; that it is the tree frog rests on Pliny’s description.

Examples

  • ea rāna, quam Graecī calamītēn vocant, quoniam inter harundinēs fruticēsque vīvat, minima omnium et viridissima

    the frog the Greeks call calamites, because it lives among reeds and bushes, the smallest and greenest of allPlin. NH 32.122

See also frog.

SourcesLewis & Short: calamites

Pliny, Naturalis Historia, ed. Mayhoff (Teubner, 1906), read in the Perseus Digital Library.
